subject: 81056F52133146DC9ED2FCA3A4D36D9E
introduction: The Bahá’í writings name Zoroaster, the Buddha and Krishna among the Manifestations of God, and say that the religions of India and the Far East began in the same truth as the others and have been overlaid, like them, with later inventions. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s remarks on the subject are scattered, mostly reported by others, and not always consistent: in one talk the Buddha founded a religion of divine unity, in a pilgrim’s note he is “a divine philosopher but not a great prophet”. The guide collects them, and the passages set beside them are from the traditions themselves: the Dhammapada and the Buddha’s last words, the Bhagavad Gítá and an Upanishad, Confucius, Lao-tzu, Kabír. A reader can then compare what is said about these religions with what they say.
questions: Reading 2 advises teaching people the truths of their own religion first. What does that require of the teacher?
The readings give different accounts of the Buddha’s station. How should reported and authenticated statements be weighed?
What do the Dhammapada and the Gítá passages have in common with the teachings the readings call universal?
The readings say these religions have decayed. Would their followers agree, and would that matter?

outside.why: Zoroaster a prophet on the pattern of the others. From the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name.
Teach them the truths in their own religion first. Paul at Athens began from the Athenians’ own altar: whom ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you.
A Buddhist asked what his religion taught. The Dhammapada: hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love.
The Buddha asked his disciples what they would do if denied and ill-treated. Let a man overcome anger by love, let him overcome evil by good.
The Founders of the various religious systems were one in purpose. The Qur’an: thou art a warner only, and for every folk a guide.
The more he acquires spiritual qualities, the nearer to perfection. The Gítá, in Edwin Arnold’s verse: let each man raise the Self by Soul, not trample down his Self.
Prophecies of this Manifestation in Buddhist books. Krishna’s promise is the best known of its kind: when Righteousness declines, I rise, from age to age.
To which category do Buddha and Confucius belong? Confucius’s own answer about himself: a transmitter and not a maker, believing in and loving the ancients.
Brahma, Krishna and Buddha never taught polytheism. The Chándogya Upanishad: only that which is, was in the beginning, one only, without a second.

“A divine philosopher but not a great prophet”, a reported remark that readings 11 and 12 contradict. The Buddha’s last counsel: be ye lamps unto yourselves; betake yourselves to no external refuge. Does a teacher who says that fit the readings’ idea of a prophet, and does it matter?
The teaching was a beautiful child and is now old. Decay is inherent in all component things.
Divinity assigned to idols and images. Kabír, from inside India: I am neither in temple nor in mosque; neither am I in rites and ceremonies.

In Turkey, Arabia and Persia nothing is thought worse than Buddhism. The verse that closes the Buddha’s parable of the blind men and the elephant: they quarrel and fight, people seeing one side. How much did the peoples named in the reading know of what they condemned, and how much do the readings themselves claim to know?
The message of Krishna is the message of love, as with all the prophets. Lao-tzu: recompense injury with kindness.
Krishna in the Gítá: whate’er thou doest, eating or sacrificing, giving gifts, praying or fasting, let it all be done for Me.

shortfall: Readings 5, 9, 10, 15, 17 to 19 and 21 are passing or reported remarks; and where the readings disagree about the Buddha’s station the companions let the Eastern texts speak for themselves.
